issues.title: Helper function missing static keyword
issues.description: The rule requires that helper functions used only within a single source file should be declared with the 'static' keyword to limit their visibility to that compilation unit. The function addHashFieldToReply is only used within t_hash.c but is declared without 'static', making it unnecessarily visible to other compilation units.
issues.rule_name: Internal Helper Functions Must Be Declared Static

issues.title: HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration time locally on master
issues.description: The hincrbyfloatCommand function is missing the HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL flag when calling hashTypeSet. While the replication command correctly uses KEEPTTL to preserve field TTL for replicas and AOF, the local execution on the master immediately removes any existing field expiration time. This creates an inconsistency where the field loses its TTL on the master but the replicated HSETEX command attempts to keep it. The test at line 1987 expects field f1 to retain its TTL after HINCRBYFLOAT, but this bug causes the TTL to be cleared locally.

issues.title: Incorrect argument count in rewriteClientCommandVector causes malformed replication
issues.description: The rewriteClientCommandVector call passes 6 as the argument count, but actually provides 7 arguments (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, value). This mismatch causes the replication command to be truncated, omitting the final argument (the new field value). Replicas and AOF will receive an incomplete HSETEX command missing the field value, leading to command execution failures on replicas, replication inconsistencies, and potential data corruption. The test expects the replication stream to contain a complete HSETEX command with all arguments.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14224 - Fix HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration on replica

structured_output.summary:
This PR is meant to fix master/replica divergence after HINCRBYFLOAT. Today the master keeps the field's TTL, but the command is replicated as plain HSET, which wipes the TTL on the replica. The fix replicates `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` instead and adds the shared objects `HSETEX` and `FIELDS` for it. The approach is right, but the change as written introduces two bugs of its own.

First, `rewriteClientCommandVector` is called with `argc = 6` but given seven arguments, so the computed value is silently dropped. Replicas and the AOF get `HSETEX h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1` with no value, which is a syntax error. Second, `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` was removed from the master's local `hashTypeSet` call, so the master now drops the field's TTL itself. That reintroduces the same divergence in reverse. There is also an unrelated change that makes `addHashFieldToReply` non-static with no declaration in any header. The new test should catch the argc bug through its replication-stream pattern. However, it never checks the TTL on the master, so it can't catch the second bug.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The wrong argc breaks replication and AOF for every HINCRBYFLOAT, and dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes the master lose field TTLs. Both are regressions in core behavior and need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
HINCRBYFLOAT is non-deterministic across float formatting, so Redis never replicates it verbatim. After running the command locally (`hashTypeSet`), `hincrbyfloatCommand` rewrites the client's argv. The propagation layer then sends the rewritten command to replicas and the AOF instead of the original. Before this PR the rewrite produced `HSET key field value`, and HSET clears any field TTL when the replica applies it.

This PR changes the rewrite to `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value`, built with `rewriteClientCommandVector` from new shared objects (`shared.hsetex`, `shared.fields`) plus the existing `shared.keepttl` and `shared.integers[1]`. On the replica, `hsetexCommand` sees `HFE_KEEPTTL` and passes `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` to `hashTypeSet`, so the field keeps its expiration. The PR also changes the flags on the master's own `hashTypeSet` call and exports `addHashFieldToReply`.
steps: Start at `hincrbyfloatCommand` in src/t_hash.c: it reads the current field value, adds the increment and formats the result with `ld2string`.
The master applies the new value with `hashTypeSet`; the flags passed here decide whether an existing field TTL is kept (`HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`).
The argv is then rewritten with `rewriteClientCommandVector` to the deterministic `HSETEX ... KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` form; the `argc` argument controls how many of the varargs end up in it.
`call()` propagates the rewritten argv to replicas and the AOF.
On the replica, `hsetexCommand` parses KEEPTTL/FIELDS and calls `hashTypeSet` with `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, keeping the field TTL.
The new test in tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl checks the replication stream format and the replica's TTLs and values.

findings.title: Wrong argc in rewriteClientCommandVector drops the value from the replicated HSETEX
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` (around lines 2571-2572) calls `rewriteClientCommandVector(c, 6, ...)` but passes 7 robj arguments (shared.hsetex, key, shared.keepttl, shared.fields, shared.integers[1], field, newobj). Because the varargs reader in `src/networking.c:4158` only consumes `argc` arguments, the value is dropped and replicas/AOF get an invalid `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field`. Change the argc to 7. Then run `./runtest --single unit/type/hash-field-expire` and confirm the replication-stream assertion `{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}` passes.

findings.title: HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL removed from the master's hashTypeSet, so the master now loses the field TTL
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand` (line ~2559) no longer passes `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` to `hashTypeSet`, so the master drops the field's TTL on HINCRBYFLOAT while the replica (via HSETEX KEEPTTL) keeps it. Restore the flag so the call is `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, matching `hincrbyCommand` at line ~2506. Also extend the new test in `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl` (~line 1996) to assert `[r -1 httl h1 FIELDS 1 f1]` is in range 90-100 on the master, and that it equals the replica's TTL.

findings.title: Test never checks the master's TTL, so master/replica divergence goes undetected
findings.body:
The test's goal is master/replica consistency, but it only checks the TTL on the replica:

::diff{file="tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl" lines="1993-2002"}

It does compare values with `hget` on both sides, but never compares `httl`. That gap is why the removed `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on the master isn't caught. Also, the comment on lines 1999-2000 ("even though it was set using HSET with KEEPTTL flag") is misleading: f2 was created with plain HSET and is only *replicated* as HSETEX KEEPTTL.

::suggestion{file="tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl" lines="1996-1997"}
                assert_range [r httl h1 FIELDS 1 f1] 90 100
                assert_range [r -1 httl h1 FIELDS 1 f1] 90 100
                assert_equal [r -1 hpexpiretime h1 FIELDS 1 f1] [r hpexpiretime h1 FIELDS 1 f1]
                assert_equal [r -1 hget h1 f1] [r hget h1 f1]
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl`, the test "HINCRBYFLOAT command won't remove field expiration on replica" (~lines 1993-2002) only checks TTLs on the replica. Add assertions that the master (`r -1`) still has a TTL on f1 after HINCRBYFLOAT, and that `hpexpiretime` on master and replica are equal for f1 and f2. Also reword the comment at ~1999-2000 to say f2 was created with plain HSET and is replicated as HSETEX KEEPTTL, which must not add a TTL.

findings.title: addHashFieldToReply made non-static with no declaration in a header
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c` line ~2576, `addHashFieldToReply` was changed from `static` to external linkage, but no header declares it and only t_hash.c uses it. Restore the `static` qualifier, since this change has nothing to do with the HINCRBYFLOAT replication fix.

findings.title: HSETEX KEEPTTL is the right replication target
findings.body: Replicating as `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` is a clean fix once the argc and flag are corrected. On the replica, `hsetexCommand` maps `HFE_KEEPTTL` to `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` (around line 2406), which keeps an existing TTL and adds none to a field that has none. The final value is still sent as a string, so float formatting can't diverge. Reusing shared objects (`shared.keepttl`, `shared.integers[1]`, the new `shared.hsetex`/`shared.fields`) avoids allocating new objects on every call.
